title: Transactional tool frames and concurrent result-injection primitives
author: Maya Patel
body: Motivation: Consumers are building increasingly complex multi-tool flows where partial tool responses are streamed back into the model (result-injection) and retries happen frequently. Current semantics around ordering, duplicate injection, and retry behavior have caused surprising non-deterministic outputs across runs and made opinionated SDK ergonomics awkward. This PR introduces a small, explicit runtime contract (transactional tool frames) and API-level ergonomics to make concurrent multi-tool calls deterministic, safe for at-most-once injection, and easier to reason about when streaming and OpenAI-compatibility layers are involved. Summary of changes: 1) Runtime primitive: ToolFrame - a compact representation (id, group, causal-set, replayable-token) attached to each tool invocation. ToolFrames are the unit of commit for result injection. 2) At-most-once injection model by default - handlers must call commit(frame_id) to make results visible to the response stream; uncommitted frames are discarded on retries unless replayable-token is present. 3) ParallelGroup and ordered-merge policies - callers can request a ParallelGroup for best-effort concurrent execution and select an ordered-merge policy (first-complete, priority-list, or deterministic-hash) to resolve injected results into structured output. 4) Retry primitives: opaque retry-tokens allow idempotent replay of tool execution when the remote tool supports it; runtime will dedupe based on replayable-token to avoid double-injection on resumed sessions. 5) SDK ergonomics: added lightweight helpers in TS/Python to create ToolFrames and await commit semantics; streaming helpers for partial injections that preserve stable chunk boundaries across reconnects. 6) OpenAI compatibility layer updates: the compatibility shim now maps the new commit/uncommit primitives to function-calls and tool call decorations so existing OpenAI-style code paths continue to work but with deterministic injection behavior. 7) Structured output: introduced a stable result-envelope schema (tool_meta + canonical_output + signatures) so downstream evals and optimizer tooling can reason about tool provenance and do targeted regressions. Migration notes: - Existing flows that assume immediate injection will continue to work but are implicitly wrapped in ephemeral ToolFrames that auto-commit on completion; this preserves compatibility for simple use cases. - Advanced users should migrate to explicit frames to get deterministic replay and better observability. Tests and validation: - Added unit tests for frame lifecycle, dedupe on replayable-token, merge-policy behavior, and fallback on partial commits. - End-to-end canary in perf-lab with mixed parallel sync/async tool stubs to validate streaming stability under reconnects. - Benchmarked overhead: average added latency per tool invocation ~0.6ms at p50; memory overhead small due to compact frame objects. Risks and mitigations: - Increased surface area for user error: made SDK helpers the default path and included lint rules in CI to prevent manual misuse. - Complexity in hybrid flows (some tools support replay, others don't): runtime falls back to at-most-once semantics and provides clear warnings in logs and console. Release notes: see release_notes field below. Detailed changelog (high-level): - runtime: add ToolFrame object, tracking and GC, commit/uncommit APIs, dedupe on replayable-token. - api: new fields in /v1/generate and tool-call payloads (frame_id, parallel_group, merge_policy, replayable_token). - sdk-ts: ToolFrame builder, commit() helper, stream-preserve middleware. - sdk-py: contextmanager ToolFrame, async commit helper, openai_shim mapping updates. - console: UI surfaces for in-flight frames, per-frame tracing and cost accounting. Related work: ENG-1248 (deterministic tool injection research), ENG-1310 (SDK ergonomics). This is intentionally small API surface with guarded defaults to preserve existing behavior while enabling deterministic concurrent tool flows for advanced workloads.
commits: Create core ToolFrame runtime + lifecycle management
Add commit/uncommit endpoints and internal dedupe map
Expose frame metadata on /v1/generate payloads and response envelopes
TS SDK: ToolFrame builder + stream-preserve middleware
Py SDK: contextmanager + async commit helper + tests
OpenAI-compat shim mapping and compatibility tests
Add console UI hooks and per-frame tracing
End-to-end perf-lab canary and CI integration tests
Docs: migration guide and API reference examples

Lena Gómez: Suggest making ordered-merge default to deterministic-hash for reproducibility. (author: set deterministic-hash as default and added examples showing priority-list override)
Tom Becker: Confirmed memory footprint under load; noted a GC path for orphaned frames. (author: added GC every 5s and metrics)
CI Bot: integration flaky on first run (timeout on perf lab) - reran, green
QA: Please add a test that simulates half-committed frames across reconnect. (author: added reconnection integration test in perf canary)
release_notes: Introduce transactional ToolFrame primitives for deterministic tool-call result injection and idempotent replay
Default at-most-once injection preserved for simple flows; advanced explicit commit API available
SDK updates (TS + Py) to simplify creation and commit of frames; minor API additions to /v1/generate
OpenAI compatibility layer updated to map function-call semantics to committed frames
